lines.text: Many learners say: If it will rain, I stay home.
Better: If it rains, I will stay home.
Rains! If it rains tomorrow, I will stay home.

data.wrong: If it will rain, I stay home.
data.right: If it rains, I will stay home.

quiz.stem: If it ___ tomorrow, I will stay home.

native.tip: Im „if“-Satz steht das Present: „If it rains“. Das „will“ kommt in den Hauptsatz.

en.hook: When do you use “will” in an “if” sentence?
en.tip: In the “if” clause use the present: “If it rains”. “Will” goes in the main clause.
en.caption: When do you use “will” in an “if” sentence? Wrong: “If it will rain, I stay home.” Right: “If it rains, I will stay home.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
